claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based alloys have high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and its single-phase fcc derivatives typically have coercivity of approximately 100 Oe or less.

Cryogenic rolling to 50–70% thickness reduction followed by annealing at 500–600 K for 1–2 hours will partially transform fcc FeCoNi-based alloys into hcp platelets or create high stacking-fault densities.
Annealing at 500–600 K stabilizes the hcp platelets and stacking-fault interfaces produced by cryogenic rolling.
Hcp platelets and stacking faults provide planar defects and fcc–hcp interfaces.
The planar defects and fcc–hcp interfaces act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning increases the coercive field.
The proposed treatment will raise coercivity above 100 Oe relative to untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative.
The proposed treatment will cause only a minimal reduction in saturation magnetization.
A processing strain of at least 50% thickness reduction is required for the expected effect.
The expected effect is bounded to annealing temperatures of 500–600 K.
Insufficient rolling strain may suppress partial hcp transformation or result in inadequate stacking-fault density.
Annealing above the proposed temperature range may suppress the partial hcp transformation or reduce stacking-fault density.
The hcp fraction, stacking-fault density, and thermal stability will vary with alloy composition and processing route.
